themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about cannabis retailers spiked to 7 THIS WEEK, up 367% from the 1.5-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting either new illegal operations opening or enforcement crackdowns triggering resident reports.
evidence: 7 cannabis retailer complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.35)
367% spike in complaints indicates sudden new activity or widespread resident concern
High statistical severity (z-score 6.35) suggests genuine anomaly, not random noise
reporting_angles: Are unlicensed cannabis retailers opening in Brownsville/Ocean Hill? Check with SLA and NYPD for enforcement activity.
Interview residents about proximity to cannabis shops and quality-of-life concerns; cross-reference with licensed dispensary locations.

themes_detail.label: Root/Sewer/Sidewalk Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Complaints about root, sewer, and sidewalk conditions surged to 4 THIS WEEK, up 700% from the 0.5-complaint weekly average, indicating possible infrastructure failure or tree root damage affecting multiple blocks.
evidence: 4 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.95)
700% spike in a single week suggests acute infrastructure event, not gradual deterioration
Converges with concurrent spike in Illegal Tree Damage (3100% spike 2 weeks ago), suggesting tree-root-driven infrastructure failure
reporting_angles: Canvass affected blocks for cracked sidewalks, exposed roots, and sewer backup; determine if single incident or district-wide pattern.
Interview DEP and Parks Dept about recent work orders, tree maintenance, and sewer condition assessments in the area.

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints peaked at 4 two weeks ago (week ending ~March 24), up 3100% from the 0.1-complaint weekly average, the highest z-score in the dataset (11.72), suggesting organized tree removal or major environmental disruption.
evidence: 4 illegal tree damage complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.72, highest on dataset)
3100% spike is the most extreme outlier in all 311 data, indicating rare, high-impact event
Likely connected to Root/Sewer/Sidewalk surge THIS WEEK, suggesting tree damage caused downstream infrastructure issues
reporting_angles: Identify which blocks experienced tree damage; visit sites to photograph and document scope. Cross-reference with Parks Dept tree inventory and removal requests.
Interview Parks Dept and NYPD about whether illegal tree cutting ring was operating; check for pattern of nighttime removals or contractor complaints.

themes_detail.label: Sewer System Stress
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints jumped to 20 LAST WEEK, up 371% from the 4.2-complaint weekly average, indicating possible overflow, backup, or system failure affecting multiple properties.
evidence: 20 sewer complaints last week vs. 4.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.7)
371% spike sustained for one full week suggests systemic issue, not isolated incident
Converges with Root/Sewer/Sidewalk complaints THIS WEEK and Illegal Tree Damage spike 2 weeks ago; pattern suggests infrastructure cascade
reporting_angles: Contact DEP about sewer main condition, recent CCTV inspections, and any known breaks or overflows in the district.
Interview residents in affected blocks about backups, odors, or water intrusions; document with photos and health impact accounts.

themes_detail.label: Street Lighting Infrastructure Gaps
themes_detail.summary: Street light condition complaints reached 12 two weeks ago, up 160% from the 4.6-complaint weekly average, suggesting systematic failure of street lighting affecting pedestrian safety and nighttime visibility.
evidence: 12 street light complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 4.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.43)
160% spike indicates concentrated outages, likely on specific corridors or near a failed transformer
Safety implication: poor street lighting correlates with increased petty crime and pedestrian accidents
reporting_angles: Map the 12 complaint locations to identify which streets/intersections are dark; assess whether outages cluster or span district.
Interview Con Edison about recent work orders, streetlight maintenance backlog, and planned repairs in CD 316.
